```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 12_independent_t_variability
title: >
  Calculate Variability
questions:
  - id: pooled_variance
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      A study compares two independent samples. Sample 1 has $n_1 = 5$ and a
      variance of $s_1^2 = 4$. Sample 2 has $n_2 = 9$ and a variance of
      $s_2^2 = 10$. What is the pooled variance, $s_p^2$?
    hint: >
      Weight each variance by its degrees of freedom, or convert each variance
      back to a sum of squares ($SS = df \times s^2$) first.
    answer: 8
    tolerance: 0.01
    explanation: >
      $SS_1 = 4 \times 4 = 16$ and $SS_2 = 8 \times 10 = 80$, so
      $s_p^2 = (16 + 80)/(4 + 8) = 96/12 = 8$. A simple average of the two
      variances would give 7. The pooled variance is closer to 10 because the
      second sample is larger, so its estimate counts for more.
```
